prompts.name: analyze_strategy
prompts.title: Analyze a strategy's returns
prompts.description: Full statistical read of a return series: quality checks, performance, risk, significance after multiple testing.

arguments.name: returns
arguments.description: The strategy's periodic returns as a JSON array (fractions).

arguments.name: trials
arguments.description: How many variants were tried before this one (for the deflated Sharpe ratio).

prompts.name: audit_backtest
prompts.title: Audit a backtest for overfitting
prompts.description: Re-run a strategy across its parameter grid and deflate the best result for the number of variants.

arguments.name: recipe
arguments.description: Strategy recipe, e.g. ma_crossover.

arguments.name: prices
arguments.description: Prices as a JSON array.

prompts.name: value_company
prompts.title: Value a company
prompts.description: Intrinsic value from cash flows, the market's implied growth, multiples and red-flag scores.

arguments.name: figures
arguments.description: The company's figures (cash flows, balance sheet, income statement) as text or JSON.

prompts.name: price_option
prompts.title: Price and risk an option
prompts.description: Check quotes, back out implied volatility, price and Greeks, and a scenario grid.

arguments.name: option
arguments.description: The option: type, strike, expiry, underlying price, rates, and the market price or chain.

prompts.name: test_mean_reversion
prompts.title: Test a spread for mean reversion
prompts.description: Stationarity, cointegration, half-life and a costed backtest of a pair or spread.

arguments.name: y
arguments.description: First price series (JSON array).

arguments.name: x
arguments.description: Second price series (JSON array), optional.

prompts.name: build_portfolio
prompts.title: Build a portfolio
prompts.description: Clean estimates, several allocations side by side, and their risk.

arguments.name: returns
arguments.description: Asset returns matrix (JSON, rows are periods).

prompts.name: analyze_trade_log
prompts.title: Analyze a trade log
prompts.description: Edge, payoff, sizing and risk of ruin from a list of trade P&Ls.

arguments.name: pnl
arguments.description: Per-trade profit and loss as a JSON array.

prompts.name: sleeve_tournament
prompts.title: Find which sleeves survive on my data
prompts.description: Run the whole sleeve library on your prices and keep only what survives multiple-testing correction.

arguments.name: prices
arguments.description: Prices: one array, or rows of columns (JSON).

arguments.name: symbols
arguments.description: Column names, e.g. ["SPY","TLT","GLD"], optional.

prompts.name: build_sleeve_book
prompts.title: Build a multi-sleeve book
prompts.description: Pick distinct surviving sleeves, combine them, and get paper-ready target weights.

arguments.name: prices
arguments.description: Prices as rows of columns (JSON).

arguments.name: symbols
arguments.description: Column names (JSON array).

prompts.name: label_dataset
prompts.title: Label a price series for machine learning
prompts.description: Annotate the data, sample events, label them, weight overlapping labels and build leak-free CV splits.

arguments.name: prices
arguments.description: Prices as a JSON array.

arguments.name: side
arguments.description: A primary model's side per period (JSON array of 1, -1, 0), optional: makes meta-labels.

prompts.name: check_dataset
prompts.title: Check a dataset before modeling
prompts.description: Run the data checks that fit the data and list every problem before any model sees it.

arguments.name: data
arguments.description: The data, or a description of it (prices, bars, option chain, curve, funding, fundamentals).

resources.name: catalog
resources.title: Tool catalog
resources.description: Every tool: name, toolset and one-line description.

resources.name: methods
resources.title: Reference checks
resources.description: What each toolset's results are checked against in the test suite.

resources.name: privacy
resources.title: Privacy guarantees
resources.description: What the server does with your data, and the tests that hold it to that.

resources.name: sleeves
resources.title: Sleeve library
resources.description: All 399 strategy sleeves: id, family, data shape, rule and spec hash.

templates.name: tool-schema
templates.title: Tool schema
templates.description: One tool's description and input JSON Schema.

templates.name: sleeve
templates.title: Sleeve spec
templates.description: One sleeve's spec, rule, rationale and references.

prompts.name: validate_backtest
prompts.title: Validate a backtest before trusting it
prompts.description: Walk through the deflated Sharpe, overfitting and track-record checks for one strategy, and report what the numbers do not establish.

arguments.name: strategy
arguments.description: What the strategy is and what data it was backtested on

arguments.name: variants_tried
arguments.description: How many variants, parameter sets or ideas were tried before this one

prompts.name: track_record_needed
prompts.title: How long a track record do I need?
prompts.description: The minimum track record length for a Sharpe to clear a benchmark, with the record's own probabilistic Sharpe if its length is known.

arguments.name: sharpe
arguments.description: The observed annualized Sharpe ratio

arguments.name: frequency
arguments.description: How often returns are measured: daily, weekly or monthly

arguments.name: benchmark
arguments.description: The annualized Sharpe it must beat; 0 if not given

arguments.name: record_length
arguments.description: How long the record already is, if known

prompts.name: backtest_and_validate
prompts.title: Backtest a rule and check whether the best variant is luck
prompts.description: Run a strategy family over a parameter grid on your prices, then read the deflated Sharpe and overfitting probability that count every variant run.

arguments.name: prices_file
arguments.description: Path to a CSV of prices on this machine

arguments.name: family
arguments.description: sma_cross, momentum, mean_reversion, breakout or buy_and_hold

prompts.name: stress_my_strategy
prompts.title: How fragile is this strategy?
prompts.description: Resampled histories and named crash, volatility, repeat and outage scenarios for a strategy's returns.

arguments.name: returns_file
arguments.description: Path to a CSV of the strategy's returns

arguments.name: drawdown_limit
arguments.description: The drawdown you could not live with, such as 0.2

prompts.name: production_check
prompts.title: Will this plan survive a real broker?
prompts.description: Order-rate and minimum-order limits, 2026 day-trading rules, market impact, crowding and capacity for a trading plan.

arguments.name: plan
arguments.description: Capital, broker, how many orders per rebalance, how often, turnover, and what it trades

prompts.name: summarize_market_series
prompts.title: Read a long series in a hundred words
prompts.description: Summarize a price or return file instead of reading its rows.

arguments.name: series_file
arguments.description: Path to a CSV of prices or returns

arguments.name: kind
arguments.description: prices or returns; default prices

prompts.name: check_signal_for_lookahead
prompts.title: Does my signal look ahead?
prompts.description: Rerun your own signal code on prefixes the server picks, and find any value that depends on later rows.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.description: Rows in the full series the signal is computed on

prompts.name: test_pipeline_on_placebos
prompts.title: Does my pipeline find edges in noise?
prompts.description: Run your whole research pipeline on placebo data, where nothing can be predicted, and see whether its real result beats what it finds there.

arguments.name: data_file
arguments.description: Path to the CSV or JSON the pipeline reads: a column per asset, dates optional

resources.name: limits
resources.title: What a result does not establish
resources.description: The boundary sentences every validation result carries.

resources.name: sources
resources.title: Sources and independent checks
resources.description: The papers behind each validator and how each is checked against them.

resources.name: strategy-spec
resources.title: Strategy families and their parameters
resources.description: JSON Schema of backtest_strategy's families, parameters and rules.

resources.name: openapi
resources.title: The validation API's OpenAPI 3.1 document
resources.description: Generated from the endpoints that exist; fetched from canlicapital.com when read.

prompts.name: known_on_date
prompts.title: What did a company report as of a date?
prompts.description: A point-in-time snapshot for a backtest or a decision: each measure as it stood on the date, the filing behind it, ratios, and which values were later restated.

arguments.name: company
arguments.description: Ticker, CIK or company name, such as AAPL

arguments.name: as_of
arguments.description: A date, YYYY-MM-DD

prompts.name: restatement_review
prompts.title: Which of a company's numbers were restated?
prompts.description: Every period whose value changed after its first report, why it changed, and the filings behind the biggest changes.

arguments.name: company
arguments.description: Ticker, CIK or company name, such as AAPL

arguments.name: concept
arguments.description: A plain name such as revenue or eps_diluted, or an XBRL tag

prompts.name: peers_as_of
prompts.title: How did peers compare as of a date?
prompts.description: One measure across several companies, each as filed by the date, with fiscal period ends lined up and later restatements flagged.

arguments.name: companies
arguments.description: Tickers or names, separated by commas, such as AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL

arguments.name: concept
arguments.description: A plain name such as revenue or eps_diluted, or an XBRL tag

arguments.name: as_of
arguments.description: A date, YYYY-MM-DD

resources.name: concepts
resources.title: Plain concept names and their XBRL tags
resources.description: Every plain name the tools accept (revenue, eps_diluted, ...), the US GAAP and IFRS tags it follows in order, and the ten known_as_of reads by default.

resources.name: limits
resources.title: What a result does not establish
resources.description: The limits every fundamentals result carries; quote them with any finding.

prompts.name: preflight_idea
prompts.title: Has this quant idea already been tried?
prompts.description: Before testing an idea: whether Canli Capital already tested it, how it was killed or survived, and what the literature says.

arguments.name: idea
arguments.description: The idea in a sentence, such as 'buy stocks after insider purchases'

prompts.name: audit_canli_record
prompts.title: How honest is Canli Capital's own record?
prompts.description: Hypotheses tried against the declared budget, the live paper record with its limits, and how to check the record was not rewritten.

prompts.name: literature_review
prompts.title: What does the research say about a topic?
prompts.description: Every Canli Capital paper on a topic, summarized with links.

arguments.name: topic
arguments.description: A topic or keyword, such as 'momentum' or 'treasury auctions'
